why: An MD run that completed, reported all three measurements with confident-looking values, and never equilibrated: `rmsd_plateau_frac` 0.18 means the backbone RMSD was still climbing for 82% of the trajectory. Nothing about the exit status, the `result`, or the three headline metrics says so -- a preorg_rmsd of 1.42 A is an entirely ordinary number. Only the integrity-role bound on `rmsd_plateau_frac` catches it, and it has to be INTEGRITY rather than acceptance (decision 0013): a measurement that did not converge is a broken instrument, so the pattern's trust must take the hit, or the next batch runs the same broken instrument. This is the label-side version of the failure the whole QC layer exists for -- and worse than the design-side version, because this number would have superseded a prediction and never been recomputed.
